summary: Morning in the Safe Cave: Bjorn wakes after Gunnar and the two male Kin have already taken care of breakfast and laundry, leaving him coffee but no obvious job.
settingText: Bushwick studio apartment, early morning: sleeping area, tiny kitchenette/table, brass key by the door, books, laundry and groceries accumulated from Issue 5.
panelPlan: Safe Cave sleeping area opening onto kitchenette — Wide: Early morning across the whole studio. Gunnar pours coffee. First Male Kin finishes slicing bread at the tiny table. Second Male Kin ties a laundry bag and checks the brass key near the door. Bjorn sits up from bedding at frame edge; Astrid is not present.
Safe Cave kitchenette table — Medium: Bjorn crosses to the table and reaches for the bread knife just as First Male Kin finishes cutting and slides the bread into a bowl.
Safe Cave doorway side of kitchenette — Medium: Bjorn turns toward the laundry bag; Second Male Kin shoulders it before Bjorn can take it.

Safe Cave kitchenette — Two-shot: Gunnar hands Bjorn a paper coffee cup. Bjorn accepts it; behind them First Male Kin clears the breakfast area and Second Male Kin settles the laundry bag on his shoulder.

Safe Cave kitchenette — Tight medium: Bjorn stands motionless with the coffee held at chest height. Behind him Gunnar turns back to the table while the two male Kin continue their tasks without looking toward Bjorn.

dialogueInline.text: That's why I left it for you.

directionInline.text: Only Gunnar, Bjorn and the two established male Kin are visible. Astrid is off-page; do not add another Kin.

summary: At the neighborhood bodega, Bjorn tries to repay old kindness with labor and is stopped because the delivery already belongs to someone else's job.
settingText: Recurring Bushwick bodega: front counter, narrow delivery aisle and sidewalk delivery area in ordinary morning light.
panelPlan: bodega front aisle — Wide: A delivery worker wheels beverage crates toward the back through the narrow aisle. Bjorn enters with his familiar coffee cup; the Bodega Owner nods from the counter.
bodega delivery aisle — Medium: The delivery worker works a loaded hand truck around a tight turn. Bjorn immediately steps toward the cart.
bodega delivery aisle — Two-shot: Before Bjorn can take the hand truck, the Bodega Owner plants one hand on it and stops him. The worker still has control of the load.
bodega delivery aisle — Three-shot: The delivery worker keeps one hand tight on the hand-truck grip, jaw set. The owner holds one forearm across Bjorn's path, leaving the worker a clear lane.
bodega counter — Close medium: The owner scans Bjorn's usual items. Bjorn stands square to the counter with direct eye contact, hands still at his sides as he answers.

dialogueInline.text: He is working. You are shopping.
You helped us before we had money.
And now you pay me every morning.
If I need help, I'll ask.
A falling roof does not ask.

directionInline.text: The delivery worker is an ordinary working adult, not comic relief and not physically helpless.

summary: Back at the apartment, Carrie hears Bjorn say plainly that everyone else now provides the things he once understood as his responsibility.
settingText: Safe Cave, late morning: table, window and ordinary household clutter from the established apartment.
panelPlan: Safe Cave doorway and table — Wide: Carrie enters with a thin folder and grocery receipt. Gunnar reads at the table. First Male Kin repairs a loose bag strap. Bjorn stands at the window with empty hands; Second Male Kin and Astrid are out.
Safe Cave table — Medium: Carrie puts the folder down and looks toward Bjorn when he does not react.
Safe Cave window side — Two-shot: Bjorn turns from the window and gives one restrained sweep of his hand toward the apartment, his face serious and still.
Safe Cave window side — Close medium: Carrie listens without correcting him. Bjorn indicates Gunnar and the working Kin with a small sweep of his hand.
Safe Cave window side — Two-shot: Carrie watches Bjorn as she says the word “ornamental.” His brow tightens at the unfamiliar word; after his reply, she supplies the simpler word “decorative.”

dialogueInline.text: Water, heat, food. Gunnar gets anywhere. They shop without us. You know every form.

directionInline.text: Only First Male Kin is visible among the Kin on this page. Second Male Kin and Astrid are off-page.

summary: A cheap power strip sparks and is already made safe before Bjorn can act; after the danger is over, he smashes it and frightens the household.
settingText: Safe Cave kitchenette and sleeping edge, daytime. Ordinary apartment scale; the electrical fault is minor and contained.
panelPlan: Safe Cave kitchenette floor beside table — Insert: A cheap overloaded power strip gives one sharp spark and a small puff of gray smoke beside the table. No flame develops.
Safe Cave kitchenette — Medium: Gunnar immediately pulls the wall plug while First Male Kin lifts nearby bedding away in one motion.
Safe Cave kitchenette — Wide: The smoke is gone. The unplugged, inert power strip lies on the floor while Carrie, Bjorn, Gunnar and both male Kin look down at it.
Safe Cave kitchenette — Medium: Bjorn bends, picks up the dead strip and stares at it. His jaw tightens; nobody is asking him to do anything.

Safe Cave bare wall beside kitchenette — Impact medium: Bjorn slams the plastic strip once into the bare wall. The casing cracks. First Male Kin jerks backward; Second Male Kin freezes with hands half-raised; Carrie flinches; Gunnar remains still with the unplugged cord.

Safe Cave kitchenette — Two-shot: Carrie steps within arm’s length of Bjorn. Behind her, First Male Kin shifts behind the table edge, Second Male Kin keeps several feet of distance, and Gunnar stays still with the unplugged cord in hand.

directionInline.text: Astrid is not visible. The electrical fault is one brief minor spark; by Panel 5 the smoke has stopped. The wall strike cracks the plastic casing once, with the household reaction carrying the impact.

summary: Carrie offers Bjorn a voluntary temporal-arrival support group, and he agrees only after she makes clear that no form, housing rule or compliance requirement is attached.
settingText: Safe Cave table, then the apartment-building stoop later the same day.
panelPlan: Safe Cave table — Medium: The cracked power strip sits inside a trash bag off to one side. Carrie and Bjorn sit across from each other with no folder between them.
Safe Cave table — Close on Carrie: After Bjorn’s immediate refusal, Carrie keeps her hands off the bare table and watches him; no paperwork sits between them.
Safe Cave table — Two-shot: Carrie puts both hands flat on the bare table while listing “No form. No compliance box. No housing condition.”
Safe Cave table — Close on Bjorn: Bjorn’s shoulders drop a fraction; his eyes move to the bagged broken power strip and then back to Carrie.
apartment-building stoop — Wide: Later, Carrie holds the building door. Bjorn comes out already dressed in his coat and passes her toward the stairs while delivering his complaint about the meeting.

dialogueInline.text: DTI has a group for arrivals.
You don't know what I'm asking.
No form. No box. No housing condition. Just people who got dropped into another time.
Talk. Argue. Sometimes sit there mad.

summary: At his first group meeting, Bjorn assumes a person from 1987 lost less than he did and is forced to confront how completely one instant can erase a life.
settingText: Plain community-center multipurpose room: mismatched stackable chairs, folding table, coffee urn, bulletin board, radiator and mixed fluorescent/daylight. No therapy-office staging.
panelPlan: community-center multipurpose room — Wide: Eight mismatched chairs make an imperfect circle. Ordinary displaced adults sit casually. Bjorn sits too upright. Group Facilitator occupies an ordinary chair, not a head position. Coffee urn and paper cups sit behind them.
community-center chair circle — Medium: 1987 Participant speaks while holding one subtle late-1980s personal object; their current clothes are practical contemporary layers.
community-center chair circle — Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn turns toward the participant, tilts his head and narrows his eyes before answering immediately.
community-center chair circle — Close on 1987 Participant: The participant's mouth tightens; they square their shoulders and hold Bjorn's gaze.
community-center chair circle — Two-shot: The participant keeps steady eye contact. Bjorn’s eyes widen slightly and his jaw relaxes; after a beat he answers the literal wording.

dialogueInline.text: Then you knew almost this world.
My brother was eight. He's sixty-two now. My parents are dead. I'm still thirty-four.

directionInline.text: Group Facilitator remains seated in the same chair circle as everyone else. Background participants wear ordinary contemporary practical clothing with no historical-costume styling.

summary: During the same meeting, Bjorn discovers that the room has firm participation rules without anyone commanding who must speak.
settingText: Same community-center multipurpose room during the first meeting.
panelPlan: Medium on Bjorn: A silence lasts. Bjorn looks from one seated participant to the next, then fixes his eyes on the facilitator.
Medium on Group Facilitator: The facilitator answers from the same kind of chair as everyone else, leaning back with hands loose on their lap.
Close on Bjorn: Bjorn leans slightly forward, brow narrowed and eyes fixed on the facilitator.
Wide: One participant drinks coffee, one looks down at folded hands, and another leans back in the chair while the silence continues.
Two-shot: After saying “But not orders,” Bjorn looks once around the circle and gives one slow nod. The facilitator remains seated and still.

summary: Bjorn correctly sees that another participant is not fine, but the facilitator stops him from turning that perception into permission to speak for them.
settingText: Same community-center multipurpose room, later in the first meeting.
panelPlan: Medium: An unnamed adult participant in ordinary contemporary clothes sits folded inward, arms close to the body, while describing an unstable housing and family situation and insisting they can manage.
Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn sits forward with brows drawn and answers immediately after the participant’s line.
Two-shot: The participant’s shoulders rise and their elbows pull inward as Bjorn says, “You fear saying so…”
Medium on Group Facilitator: The facilitator remains seated and raises one hand toward Bjorn as they say, “Stop.”
Tight two-shot: The facilitator keeps one hand raised toward Bjorn and turns the other open palm toward the participant as the exchange continues.

dialogueInline.speaker: OTHER PARTICIPANT
dialogueInline.text: It's fine. I can handle it.
You're afraid if you say it, someone decides for you.
Maybe. It's still theirs to say.

directionInline.text: The unnamed participant is an ordinary adult and remains visually separate from the recurring 1987 Participant.

summary: After the meeting, Carrie sees that Bjorn intends to return because he leaves still arguing with the facilitator instead of dismissing the room.
settingText: Community-center hallway and front sidewalk immediately after the first meeting.
panelPlan: community-center hallway — Wide: Carrie waits on a bench scrolling work messages. The meeting-room door opens and participants filter out normally.
community-center doorway — Two-shot: Bjorn exits while facing backward toward the facilitator inside, continuing the argument as he walks.
community-center hallway — Medium on Carrie and Bjorn: Carrie matches Bjorn’s stride and looks sideways at him; one corner of her mouth twitches before she asks her question.
community-center front sidewalk — Wide: Bjorn and Carrie keep walking. The facilitator remains in the doorway and calls after him; Bjorn answers without turning back.

dialogueInline.text: If a roof falls, you don't ask first.

summary: At home, Bjorn nearly settles an argument between the two male Kin, stops himself, and asks whether they want his decision or only his judgment.
settingText: Safe Cave, afternoon: tool storage area and lease-painted wall.
panelPlan: Safe Cave wall and freestanding shelf — Wide: First Male Kin holds a small wooden tool rack against the painted wall while Second Male Kin points toward the freestanding shelf instead. A drill and small hardware sit nearby.
Safe Cave wall — Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn enters, looks from the rack against the wall to the drill in Second Male Kin’s hand, and raises one hand as his first word starts.
Safe Cave wall — Close on Bjorn: He stops in the middle of the first word and lowers the hand slightly.
Safe Cave wall — Three-shot: Bjorn asks what role they actually want from him. The two men exchange a quick look before First Male Kin answers.

Safe Cave wall and shelf — Wide: Bjorn looks from the landlord-painted drywall to the rack and then to the freestanding shelf before pointing at the shelf. Second Male Kin lowers the drill to the floor.

dialogueInline.text: Do you want me to decide?
No. Tell me what you think.
Then use the shelf. Don't put holes in the wall.

directionInline.text: Show exactly the two established male Kin. Astrid is absent; do not add a third Kin.

summary: On the stairs, Bjorn catches the Upstairs Neighbor before a fall without waiting to be asked, then learns that immediate safety does not give him ownership of the rest of her task.
settingText: Fifth-floor stair landing and hallway outside apartment 5B.
panelPlan: fifth-floor stair landing — Wide: The Upstairs Neighbor climbs the last steps carrying a full laundry basket. One foot slips on the stair edge and the basket tips forward.
fifth-floor stair landing — Medium: Bjorn moves instantly, catching the neighbor by the forearm with one hand and steadying the basket with the other before either person or laundry falls.
fifth-floor landing — Two-shot: The neighbor regains her footing and takes the basket back against her hip. Bjorn reaches toward it as if to take the load.
fifth-floor landing — Two-shot: She keeps hold of the basket and gives him a flat look while Bjorn stops reaching.
fifth-floor hallway — Wide: The neighbor walks toward her door under her own power. Bjorn remains by the stairs, watching her go without following.

dialogueInline.text: No. Catching me helped. I'm keeping the laundry.

summary: Bjorn overcorrects by waiting for an invitation to do ordinary shared household work, and Gunnar points out that restraint is not the same thing as becoming passive in his own home.
settingText: Safe Cave doorway, kitchenette and table during an ordinary grocery return.
panelPlan: Safe Cave doorway — Wide: Gunnar and the two male Kin enter with several grocery bags. Bjorn sits at the table, sees the load and deliberately keeps both hands where they are.
Safe Cave main room — Medium on Bjorn and Gunnar: Gunnar sets two heavy bags on the floor beside Bjorn's chair and looks at him. Bjorn looks from the bags to Gunnar but does not move.
Safe Cave table — Two-shot: Gunnar answers while First Male Kin carries bread toward the kitchenette and Second Male Kin puts a bag on the counter.
Safe Cave kitchenette — Wide: Bjorn stands, takes the two bags from the floor and begins putting his share of the groceries away with the others.
Safe Cave kitchenette — Two-shot: Gunnar passes behind Bjorn with another bag and delivers the correction without stopping. Bjorn pauses, then continues unpacking.

directionInline.text: Show exactly the two established male Kin with Gunnar and Bjorn. Astrid is off-page.

summary: At the bodega, Bjorn finds no debt to repay and no labor to perform; the owner simply gives him his usual coffee and lets ordinary familiarity be enough.
settingText: Recurring bodega front counter during a quiet morning lull.
panelPlan: bodega front counter — Wide: The store is quiet between customers. The Bodega Owner pours Bjorn's usual coffee while Bjorn automatically scans the aisle, delivery stack and counter for work that might need doing.
bodega front counter — Two-shot: The owner notices Bjorn looking past him toward the back aisle and slides the coffee across.
bodega counter — Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn takes the cup but continues looking around the shop as if a task must be hiding somewhere.
bodega counter — Two-shot: The owner leans one forearm on the counter and asks about the promotional toaster. Bjorn finally looks at him instead of at the work.
bodega front counter — Wide: Bjorn stands drinking coffee while the owner checks a receipt. Neither man needs anything from the other for the moment.

summary: Carrie arrives to escort Bjorn to the next meeting and learns he already left alone because Gunnar showed him the route once.
settingText: Apartment doorway, Safe Cave interior and a brief view of the block outside.
panelPlan: fifth-floor hallway at apartment 5B — Medium: Carrie knocks once and enters with her coat still on, one hand already gesturing back toward the hallway as she calls for Bjorn.

Safe Cave interior — Wide: Gunnar reads at the table. First Male Kin tightens a strap on a household bag. Bjorn, Astrid and Second Male Kin are absent; after Carrie calls, neither Gunnar nor First Male Kin looks toward the door.
Safe Cave table — Medium on Carrie and Gunnar: Carrie scans the empty window and sleeping side of the studio where Bjorn would normally be, then looks back to Gunnar.
Safe Cave table — Two-shot: Carrie points her thumb toward the hallway as she asks whether Bjorn left alone. Gunnar turns one page before replying.

Bushwick sidewalk half a block from apartment — Long medium: Bjorn walks alone half a block from the apartment through ordinary pedestrian traffic, coat closed and pace steady toward the community center.

dialogueInline.text: You showed him the route once.
That is not the reassuring part.

summary: At the next meeting, the 1987 Participant asks about a family dinner; Bjorn stops before deciding for them, asks what they actually want, and offers a boundary and an exit instead of a verdict.
settingText: Community-center multipurpose room during Bjorn's next support-group meeting.
panelPlan: Wide: The next meeting is already underway. The 1987 Participant sits across from Bjorn; the facilitator is visible in the same ordinary chair as everyone else.
Medium on 1987 Participant: The participant describes the family dinner problem with irritation rather than panic.
Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn starts to answer immediately, stops after two words, then resets and asks a different question.
Two-shot: The participant answers without looking at the facilitator. Bjorn listens through the whole sentence.
Two-shot: Bjorn gives the narrowest advice he can: state the boundary before arriving and leave if the bargain changes.
Close on participant then Bjorn: The participant asks whether that means they should go. Bjorn refuses to turn the boundary into a command.

dialogueInline.text: My brother wants me at dinner. Last time they asked about music and Reagan all night.
If they do it anyway, leave.

summary: The 1987 Participant points out that either choice can still hurt; Bjorn admits he cannot make the decision painless, learning that respecting agency does not guarantee a clean outcome.
settingText: Same community-center multipurpose room during the same meeting.
panelPlan: Medium on 1987 Participant: The participant does not let Bjorn's boundary advice end the problem.
Two-shot: Bjorn listens. The facilitator watches from the side without stepping in.
Close on Bjorn: Bjorn looks down for a beat instead of producing a faster answer.
Medium on 1987 Participant: The participant pushes because the answer is unsatisfying.
Two-shot: Bjorn accepts the inadequacy of his answer rather than turning it into an order.
Wide: The participant leans back and makes their own choice. Bjorn nods once; the facilitator says nothing.

dialogueInline.text: If I leave, my brother thinks I rejected them. If I stay, I become the story again.
I don't know how to make it cheaper.
Then I go. If it starts, I leave.

summary: After the meeting, Bjorn and the facilitator agree that adults need ways to contribute and clash over whether contribution should ever become the price of care.
settingText: Community-center multipurpose room during cleanup, then hallway.
panelPlan: community-center multipurpose room after meeting — Wide: Participants stack cups and chairs. Bjorn folds one chair and adds it to the same stack while two other participants clean nearby.
community-center multipurpose room — Two-shot: Bjorn and the facilitator continue their argument while carrying chairs toward the wall.
community-center multipurpose room — Medium on facilitator: The facilitator keeps carrying a folded chair toward the wall while answering Bjorn.
community-center multipurpose room — Two-shot: Bjorn stops his folded chair against the wall and turns to face the facilitator. The facilitator sets their own chair beside it while answering him.
community-center hallway — Wide: They walk in opposite directions down the hallway, both still wearing tight, irritated expressions.

dialogueInline.text: If nobody needs you, what do you do all day?
If people feed you and ask nothing, what are you giving back?
Why does care have to be a trade?
That's you. Don't make it everyone.

summary: Carrie vents about a DTI deadline mess, and Bjorn asks whether she wants counsel or only a witness before offering any solution.
settingText: Neighborhood coffee cart and nearby sidewalk bench in late afternoon.
panelPlan: sidewalk beside neighborhood coffee cart — Medium: Carrie walks beside Bjorn with coffee and a folder tucked under one arm, already mid-rant.
sidewalk beside coffee cart — Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn walks beside Carrie with brows knit, eyes fixed on her and both hands empty and still while she continues.
sidewalk — Two-shot: Bjorn raises one hand slightly and asks his question before Carrie reaches the next complaint.
sidewalk — Two-shot: Carrie stops for half a step and turns to look directly at Bjorn. He meets her eye and repeats the question.
sidewalk walking away from coffee cart — Two-shot: They resume walking. Carrie says “Witness.” Bjorn delivers one sentence, then goes silent while she answers “Thank you.”

dialogueInline.text: He changed the deadline, emailed me the old one, then asked why I was confused.
Now I have to explain dates to a man with three calendars.
You want me to fix it?
You want me to say he's an idiot?

summary: At home, Bjorn notices that he no longer knows every route and errand in the household and chooses not to demand an inventory.
settingText: Safe Cave, early evening as people return from separate routines.
panelPlan: Safe Cave main room — Wide: Gunnar reads at the table. First Male Kin repairs a bag. Second Male Kin enters carrying a small purchase; Bjorn’s eyes widen briefly and track him across the room. Astrid is not present.
Safe Cave doorway — Medium on Bjorn: After the door closes, Bjorn glances from Gunnar to First Male Kin, then Second Male Kin, then back to the empty doorway.
Safe Cave table — Two-shot: Gunnar catches Bjorn looking toward the empty doorway and looks up from his book.
Safe Cave table — Two-shot: Bjorn turns his head toward the empty doorway while saying he does not know where everyone is. Gunnar answers without looking up from the book.
Safe Cave main room — Wide: Bjorn looks once more across the room, then lowers himself onto a chair near the wall. The doorway remains quiet.

dialogueInline.text: I don't know where everyone is.

directionInline.text: Astrid is off-page. Only First Male Kin and Second Male Kin appear among the Kin.

summary: The Bodega Owner trusts Bjorn to stand watch at the counter for two minutes, giving him responsibility based on presence and judgment rather than physical strength.
settingText: Recurring bodega front counter near closing time.
panelPlan: Wide: The Bodega Owner has a delivery invoice in one hand and gestures toward the basement door behind the counter while Bjorn stands with his usual coffee.
Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn takes position beside the counter with absurd formality while the owner disappears downstairs. He keeps both hands off the register.
Medium: A familiar neighborhood customer enters, takes a coffee, leaves exact cash on the counter and gives Bjorn a casual nod before leaving. Bjorn watches but does not interfere.
Two-shot: The owner returns with the invoice and glances around the unchanged store.
Two-shot: Bjorn reports the transaction as if delivering a watch report. The owner accepts it without ceremony.

dialogueInline.text: Maria took coffee. Left two dollars.
You were here. That's what I needed.

summary: Before another meeting, the 1987 Participant tells Bjorn that the dinner went badly, they left on their own terms, and their brother later invited them back under better ones.
settingText: Sidewalk outside the community center and the entry corridor before a later meeting.
panelPlan: community-center sidewalk — Wide: Bjorn approaches alone. 1987 Participant waits by the door holding a takeout container, keys and phone visible in the other hand, coat open over ordinary contemporary clothes.
community-center sidewalk — Two-shot: The participant lifts the takeout container slightly while saying “I went.” Bjorn stops in front of them and waits for the rest.
community-center doorway — Medium on 1987 Participant: The participant opens both hands at “They did it again,” then hooks a thumb toward the street while saying “I left.”

community-center entry corridor — Two-shot walking: They enter side by side. The participant taps the phone in one hand while mentioning the next-day call; Bjorn turns his head toward them for “Better terms.”

dialogueInline.text: They did it again. Questions, jokes. My brother told them to stop. They didn't. I left.
He called the next day. Asked me back. Just us.

summary: At a later meeting, Bjorn stops analyzing everyone else and says his own fear aloud: if nobody needs his protection, he does not know his place.
settingText: Community-center multipurpose room during a later support-group meeting.
panelPlan: Wide: A normal silence settles over the group. Bjorn sits with both hands flat on his knees and his eyes fixed on the floor.
Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn lifts his head, draws one breath and raises two fingers slightly from his knee before speaking.
Wide reaction: Several participants glance up but remain in their chairs. The facilitator keeps the same seated posture while answering “Okay.”
Close on Bjorn: Bjorn holds the facilitator’s gaze, jaw relaxed, with both hands flat on his knees as he speaks.
Two-shot: The facilitator remains still through the answer. Bjorn’s brow furrows after the first sentence and he tilts his head before replying.

dialogueInline.text: If they don't need me to protect them, I don't know what I do.
Maybe it doesn't have to be.

summary: Back home, Bjorn offers help once, accepts a no without injury, and then contributes to a shared household routine without waiting to be invited; Gunnar later asks for his judgment.
settingText: Safe Cave, evening, with ordinary repair, groceries, coffee and library books in progress at the same time.
panelPlan: Safe Cave main room — Wide: Gunnar compares two library books. First Male Kin works on a stubborn clamp. Second Male Kin sorts groceries. Bjorn enters and sees all three tasks at once.
Safe Cave repair area — Two-shot: Bjorn stops beside First Male Kin instead of reaching for the tool.

Safe Cave kitchenette — Medium: Bjorn accepts the no immediately, moves to the kitchenette and starts the household coffee without asking whether anyone needs it. Second Male Kin silently sets out cups beside him.
Safe Cave table — Medium on Gunnar and open book: Gunnar turns an illustrated page toward Bjorn while Bjorn pours the first cup.

Safe Cave main room — Wide: First Male Kin keeps his own tool, Second Male Kin continues groceries, Gunnar leaves the book open for later, and Bjorn finishes pouring coffee: participating without owning anyone else's task.

dialogueInline.text: When you're done, look at this picture.

directionInline.text: Show exactly the two established male Kin. Astrid is not visible on this page.

summary: Late that night, the household continues several separate routines around Bjorn, and he answers Carrie's question about the group by saying, 'There is work here.'
settingText: Safe Cave, late evening: window, table and whole-room geography with everyone returning to ordinary separate routines.
panelPlan: Safe Cave whole room — Wide: Gunnar reads. First Male Kin continues a small repair while Second Male Kin sorts groceries. Astrid enters in the background carrying one small bag; First Male Kin gives her a brief nod and Second Male Kin shifts aside to let her pass. Carrie sits at the table with coffee, no folder visible. Bjorn stands near the window.
Safe Cave table/window axis — Medium on Carrie: Carrie looks toward Bjorn and asks about the group without getting up from the table.
Safe Cave window — Medium on Bjorn: Bjorn turns one shoulder and his head slightly toward Carrie, expression grave.
Safe Cave table — Medium on Carrie: Carrie lifts one eyebrow, delivers her reply and takes another sip of coffee.

Safe Cave whole room — Bjorn POV wide: Bjorn looks across the room: repair, books, groceries, Astrid putting away her bag, Carrie resting. Everyone continues their activity without looking toward him for direction.

Safe Cave window with room behind Bjorn — Tight medium: Bjorn faces Carrie in the foreground. Behind him Gunnar keeps reading, the two male Kin continue their separate tasks, and Astrid puts away the small bag as he answers.

directionInline.text: Astrid’s return remains background business: one small bag, no explanation dialogue, and no special reaction from the household.
